title: Preserving our Heritage, Culture and History –  Conserving Dakota Crescent
what_it_is: Preserving our Heritage, Culture and History –  Conserving Dakota Crescent

sections.label: Rochor Centre demolition announced
sections.summary: In 2011, LTA announced Rochor Centre would be demolished for the new North South Expressway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In 2011, LTA announced that Rochor Centre would be demolished to make way for the new North South Expressway.

sections.label: Volunteering at Rochor Centre
sections.summary: The speaker began volunteering as a grassroots leader at Rochor Centre and is sad the four multi-coloured blocks will disappear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It was at Rochor Centre that I started volunteering as a grassroots leader because I wanted to improve the condition of the estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It saddens me that the four multi-coloured blocks of flats which carry 40 years of memories for those residents would disappear soon.

sections.label: Urgent action for local heritage
sections.summary: Without urgent action to evaluate what and how to preserve local heritage, culture and identity, these memories may be lost forever.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If Singapore does not take urgent action to evaluate what to preserve and how to preserve our local heritage, culture and identity, these memories may be lost forever.

sections.label: Reconsider Dakota Crescent redevelopment
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to reconsider its plans for redeveloping Dakota Crescent in Mountbatten constituency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: How can we recall our past with nostalgia?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I wish to call on the Government to reconsider its plans for redeveloping Dakota Crescent which is within Mountbatten constituency.

sections.label: Dakota Crescent flats built by SIT
sections.summary: Dakota Crescent was built in 1958 by the Singapore Improvement Trust, with 10 seven-storey, four three-storey and one two-storey blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Dakota Crescent was built in 1958 by the Singapore Improvement Trust (SIT), the predecessor of HDB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There are 10 blocks of seven-storey flats, four blocks of three storey flats and one block of two storey flats.

sections.label: Dove-shape marble playground
sections.summary: A dove-shape marble playground sits in the estate and the speaker was told it is the only one left in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the midst of the estate sits a dove-shape marble playground which I was told is the only dove-shape playground left in Singapore.

sections.label: Residents' Conservation Report to URA
sections.summary: Residents laboured for many months and prepared a Conservation Report to URA and the National Heritage Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The group of residents whom I talked to laboured for many months and they have prepared a Conservation Report to URA and the National Heritage Board.

sections.label: Wychwood Barns community reopening
sections.summary: Wychwood Barns reopened in 2008 and hosts artist spaces, non-profit facilities, studios, gardens, a gallery and a covered street.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Wychwood Barns reopened in 2008 and has become the "social heart" of the community, hosting 26 artist live­work spaces, programming and administrative facilities for 10 non-profit organisations, 14 artists' studios, indoor and outdoor community gardens, a community-run gallery and an 8,000-square feet covered street used for farmers and art markets, conference and events.

sections.label: Cultural assets in urban planning
sections.summary: The speaker urges Government and urban planners to treat cultural assets as a development resource and move towards cultural planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I would counter that by arguing that these cannot replace the role and power of actual sites, resplete with their stories, lessons learnt and hopes for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government and urban planners to embrace cultural assets as a resource for development and, in considering adaptive uses for them, move from just urban planning towards cultural planning.

sections.label: Dakota Crescent redevelopment proposal
sections.summary: Mr Lim's proposal is a ground-up initiative with a bold vision to redevelop Dakota inclusively while respecting its heritage and community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposal that Mr Lim had presented earlier is exactly what the Government has always been looking for – ground-up initiative with a bold vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposal requires us to work with many different communities within and outside of Dakota, to redevelop the place into something inclusive, yet deeply respectful of the heritage and community of Dakota Crescent.

sections.label: Ground-up Dakota redevelopment initiative
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider the community's proposal to redevelop and repurpose Dakota, calling it potentially pioneering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a ground-up initiative by a community that seeks to strengthen itself and remain relevant to our nation's narrative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would therefore urge the Government to consider this proposal positively, to give residents the opportunity to redevelop and repurpose Dakota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Page: 72 What we have is a potentially pioneering project that could become a milestone in our approach towards urban and community development, one where the people take ownership and proactively negotiate amongst themselves to put forward viable, sustainable plans for the future.

sections.label: Conserved areas and historical buildings
sections.summary: Singapore has conserved Historic Districts, pre-World War II Tiong Bahru flats, and historical buildings such as Queenstown Public Library and Alexandra Hospital.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, we have conserved large areas, such as the Historic Districts of Chinatown, Kampong Glam, Little India and Singapore River.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have retained several pre-World War II residential flats in Tiong Bahru built by SIT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have also conserved many historical buildings which are representative of our rich architectural heritage and bear testimony to the history and development of Singapore, such as the Queenstown Public Library and the key buildings of the Alexandra Hospital.

sections.label: NHB tangible heritage survey
sections.summary: NHB has recently started a tangible heritage survey to build on its existing database of heritage resources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In addition, NHB has recently embarked on a tangible heritage survey to build on NHB's existing database of heritage resources.

sections.label: Balestier state land sale conditions
sections.summary: A 2008 Balestier state land sale for a hotel required the developer to provide a public park at the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall entrance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: When a parcel of state land at Balestier was sold in 2008 for a hotel development, the sales conditions included requirements for the developer to provide a public park at the entrance to the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.

sections.label: UNESCO awards for Singapore restoration
sections.summary: Since 2001, several restoration projects in Singapore have received UNESCO Asia-Pacific Cultural Heritage Conservation Awards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Since 2001, a number of restoration projects in Singapore have been conferred UNESCO Asia-Pacific Cultural Heritage Conservation Awards.

sections.label: National monuments and conserved buildings
sections.summary: Singapore has more than 70 national monuments and more than 7,000 conserved buildings, which many Singaporeans do not realise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Not many Singaporeans realise this, but there are more than 70 national monuments on our island and more than 7,000 conserved buildings dot our cityscape.

sections.label: NHB Dakota Crescent research project
sections.summary: NHB commissioned a research project in April last year to document Dakota Crescent's history, including community landmarks and architecturally interesting buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, NHB commissioned a research project in April last year to document the history of the Dakota Crescent area, including key community landmarks and buildings of architectural interest.

sections.label: Engaging on Dakota Crescent proposals
sections.summary: The government looks forward to receiving Dakota Crescent proposals and will engage Mr Lim, the heritage community and groups to plan sensitively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We understand that the residents and the heritage community who are passionate about conserving Dakota Crescent have been working on proposals, and when Mr Lim Biow Chuan showed the set of documents, we see it for the first time, although from a distance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We look forward to receiving these suggestions and will engage Mr Lim, members of the Heritage Community and the various groups that have worked on this project, to come up with a plan that is sensitive to the character and heritage of Dakota, while keeping our eye to the future.
